page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Below the text, centred: the heading "EXERC. X." and a title in italic capitals and italic. Then a new paragraph with a large initial Q. Small "»" marks stand at the right edge beside the lines of that paragraph. Gathering signature "C 5" at the lower left, with the catchword "subiun-" at the lower right.

main_text.l: enim soles, quot corpora, in quae agit, ipse
produceret. Sic neq; ignis lignu, quod urit,
in sui naturam, sed in cinere mutat. Calcea-
rius item corium in quod agit, in se nequa-
quam uertit. Sunt (ut summatim dicam ) &
alia pene innumera agentia, quae sua in se
nō uertunt subiecta. Igitur hoc Fernelij ef-
fatum, nō simpliciter, sed distinctè, & qua-
tenus fieri potest, intelligitur. Nam agens
naturale subiectum, quod quidem est hoc
fieri natum aptum, in quod agit, conuertit.
Panis utiq; in sanguinem ab animalis calo-
re, deinde in carne mutari potest: quoniam
ille est caro potentia, hoc est, potentiam in
se habet, per quam a naturali calore sic mu-
tari potest. Quoniam autem hac potestate
carent lapides, ideo nulla caloris animalis
ui in sanguinem, ac tandem in carnem con-
uerti queunt.

page.notes: The "»" marks at the right edge beside the lines "forma extrinsecus assumi a subiecto, cum ijs cohaerere non uidentur" are not printed text, so they are left out. The heading mark "A'" is read as an apostrophe with [?] omitted, as it is clearly printed. Long s has been rendered as s throughout, so "eft" appears as "est" and "fubiecto" as "subiecto". The printed "fui" in line 3 is read as "sui" and the "s" forms in the heading follow the same rule. The printed "nó" is read as "nō" with a macron. No other doubtful readings.
